divergences.published_php: Keyed signal and update receipts do not echo the caller request_id or identify fresh admission with retained false and intent_verified true.
divergences.native: Fresh keyed admissions echo the literal caller key with retained false and intent_verified true. Retained receipts echo the same key and retain their existing intent-proof markers, including false for legacy receipts without a digest.
divergences.harness: The signals-before-worker comparator requires exact metadata only on its keyed admission. Update validation requires exact caller keys and fresh markers on approved/plain/completed-wait admissions and preserves true/false intent evidence on retained approval/raw-key rejection. Every original receipt field and all other responses remain exact. Frozen PHP fixtures and observations are unchanged.

divergences.published_php: A retained update receipt has no explicit retained or intent_verified fields.
divergences.native: Retried update receipts explicitly identify retention and whether a recorded intent proves equality. A pre-intent legacy receipt is returned with intent_verified false rather than fabricated equality.
divergences.harness: The update-validation contract requires retained true and intent_verified true on native's retained approval, and retained true with intent_verified false on the raw-key rejection that has no digest. Original receipt fields, PHP recordings and frozen fixtures are unchanged. Legacy unverified readback, ambiguity and zero writes are covered by all-backend execution regressions.

divergences.published_php: The limits object does not advertise a separate workflow task completion request-body budget.
divergences.native: limits.max_workflow_task_completion_bytes advertises the actual enforced wire-request cap for workflow and activity continuation completions, independently of per-value limits.
divergences.harness: The native cluster-info comparator requires the exact field and shared-vector default value. PHP and embedded observations and frozen fixtures remain unchanged. Actual HTTP boundary and TCP refusal tests consume the shared completion-limit vectors.

divergences.published_php: A scheduled, backfilled or drained schedule occurrence starts its run under a generated ULID workflow id.
divergences.native: As embedded mode (Workflow 2.15.15 and later, PhpClassScheduleStarter::instanceId), an occurrence's run id is schedule.ns:{sha256(namespace), 32 hex}:{byte length}:{schedule_id}:backfill:{unix seconds}, with the schedule id replaced by h:{sha256(schedule_id)} when the id would exceed 191 characters or leave [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. A repeated fire of an occurrence whose run exists is skipped as already_fired_occurrence. Manual triggers keep generated ids.
divergences.harness: Schedule normalization treats the deterministic form as a volatile identity, as it does ULIDs, and the catalog and dispatch-summary checks accept it for the native target only. PHP and embedded observations and frozen fixtures remain unchanged. All-backend execution tests cover ordinary, backfilled, namespaced, hashed and repeated occurrences.

divergences.published_php: limits.max_operation_name_length advertises the configured DW_MAX_OPERATION_NAME_LENGTH, 256 by default, though signal and update names are stored in 255-character columns.
divergences.native: Signal, update and query names are capped at 255 bytes, the column size, with the typed 422 validation_failed naming signal_name, update_name or query_name; limits.max_operation_name_length advertises 255. DW_MAX_OPERATION_NAME_LENGTH still refuses any value but its default, so the cap cannot be raised or disabled.
divergences.harness: The native cluster-info comparator requires 255 for this one limit. PHP and embedded observations and frozen fixtures remain unchanged. The all-backend execution tests cover the 255-byte boundary and the refusal.

divergences.published_php: Every storage driver failure, including a refused permission, is the retryable external payload storage unavailable outcome, and the transport manifest lists no access-denied outcome.
divergences.native: A storage permission refusal (EACCES or EPERM from the local driver) is external_payload_storage_access_denied: 424, retryable false, with a constant message and no storage location, on the transport upload and fetch, workflow start, worker task completion and the storage diagnostic, which also names the failed step (put, get or delete). Any other storage failure stays external_payload_unavailable, 503 and retryable. The transport manifest's typed_outcomes lists the new outcome.
divergences.harness: The native cluster-info comparator requires the one added typed outcome. PHP and embedded observations and frozen fixtures remain unchanged. All-backend execution tests cover access refusal and outage on the transport fetch, workflow start, worker task completion and each storage diagnostic step.

divergences.published_php: Registrations are kept until deregistration or namespace deletion, and GET /api/workers returns every registration in the namespace, newest heartbeat first, with no limit.
divergences.native: A registration with no heartbeat for DW_WORKER_REGISTRATION_RETENTION_SECONDS (default 86400, never less than the stale window) is deleted unless it holds an unexpired task lease. GET /api/workers returns at most 100 registrations in worker id order with page_size (1 to 100), next_page_token and registration_retention_seconds; 422 invalid_page_size and 400 invalid_page_token refuse a bad page request.
divergences.harness: The worker-listing comparator checks each listed worker and the stale window and does not depend on order or extra top-level fields, so it is unchanged. Its recording registers two workers, well under one page, and none ages past retention. The all-backend execution tests cover paging, expiry, retained draining, recently stale and lease-holding workers, and pinned-build diagnostics after expiry.

divergences.published_php: Published PHP does not admit timeout cleanup on service starts, and embedded Workflow 2.29.0 run detail and describe show neither the cleanup state nor its outcome; the outcome is visible only on the terminal history event and in the timeout failure message.
divergences.native: Describe and run detail of an opted-in run carry timeout_cleanup {state: armed | cancellation_cleanup_running | finished | not_entered, cause (timeout once entered), allowance_seconds, timeout_kind, work_deadline_at, cleanup_deadline_at, started_at, outcome, failure_id}. A run without the opt-in has no timeout_cleanup key.
divergences.harness: No recorded corpus run opts in, so no comparator changes. The all-backend execution tests cover every state and outcome.

divergences.published_php: Embedded Workflow 2.29.0 has no child-workflow timeout cleanup option; the portable contract gives a child its own timeouts and its own opt-in.
divergences.native: start_child_workflow accepts timeout_cleanup_seconds under the start's admission rules (1 to 86400, a child timeout required, shorter than each one, a live capable worker on the child's queue); the child records its own WorkflowStarted.timeout_cleanup, and a retried child keeps its allowance. The parent's allowance never carries over.
divergences.harness: No recorded corpus command carries the field. The all-backend execution tests cover validation, capability refusal without writes, and the child's recorded allowance.

divergences.published_php: An update retried under an existing request_id with different arguments returns the original receipt.
divergences.native: The same retry is refused with 409 request_id_conflict (outcome rejected_request_id_conflict) and writes nothing. A retry with the original arguments returns the original receipt.
divergences.harness: Against native, the state-updates and update-validation probes first prove the conflict and then retry with the original arguments; the SDK direction drivers retry with the original arguments, and the direction contract expects them. PHP and embedded recordings are unchanged.

divergences.published_php: A run its own code closes (complete, fail, continue as new) leaves its open activities and timers as they are; nothing is recorded for them.
divergences.native: As Core workflow#1117 (Workflow 2.28.0), the close records ActivityCancelled (cancellation_reason run_closed) for each open activity and TimerCancelled for each pending timer, wait timeouts included, before the terminal event, and appends nothing after it.
divergences.harness: Each affected fixture section names this divergence and carries a reviewed native_expected that overlays only the changed steps of its published expected; the contracts apply it for the native target alone. PHP and embedded recordings are unchanged.

divergences.published_php: Disabling new external writes also prevents deletion through that namespace policy; a sole payload keeps its run until the policy is enabled again.
divergences.native: Each admitted object retains its original validated local storage binding. Disabling new writes does not prevent retention cleanup; the sole payload and run details are deleted and a later explicit prune observes run_not_found.
divergences.harness: The two named retention steps and three named namespace-deletion steps have exact native-only expectations. Re-enabling an already deleted namespace returns 404; shared-object and unused-registration counts remain exact. Every original PHP setup/step remains byte-equivalent as data; held and peer objects, deletion counts, cleanup inventory and final fetch are still required. No storage outage, unavailable original binding or pending cleanup is accepted as a successful deletion.

divergences.published_php: Queries on failed, cancelled and terminated runs are refused with 409 run_not_active; completed is the only closed status that is queried. A run whose history retention pruned is not refused before a worker claims it.
divergences.native: A retained run of any status, including failed, cancelled and terminated, is queried read-only on its original run, as embedded WorkflowStub::queryWithArguments replays any run: the same run binding, route and authority fences, with no history or status change. A run whose history retention pruned, or whose WorkflowStarted event is missing, is refused with 409 query_history_unavailable, history_state pruned or missing, run_status and is_terminal, and admits no query task. The query control-plane contract lists that reason after run_not_active.
divergences.harness: The waterline-import comparator requires query_history_unavailable once, right after run_not_active, in each native query contract and then compares the rest exactly. Published PHP and embedded observations and frozen fixtures remain unchanged. The all-backend execution tests cover completed, failed, cancelled and terminated runs, instance- and run-targeted queries, unchanged history, and pruned and missing history.

divergences.published_php: A child still open when its parent continues as new stays with the closed predecessor: no run of the chain applies its parent-close policy, and a later failure of the child is never retried.
divergences.native: As Core workflow#868 and workflow#1107 (Workflow 2.26.0), the continued run supervises each open child in the continue-as-new transaction. The chain's final run applies its request_cancel, terminate or request_cancellation policy to the child's current run when it closes and records ParentClosePolicyApplied or ParentClosePolicyFailed (and ParentCloseCancellationRequested) in its own history. A child that fails while a run of the chain supervises it is retried under its recorded retry policy, and nothing is appended to the closed predecessor. A chain continued before this change keeps the published behavior.
divergences.harness: No shared fixture closes a chain that continued over an open non-abandon child or fails such a child afterward, so no fixture section names this divergence and every PHP and embedded recording is unchanged. The all-backend native execution suite (child_supervision) covers the behavior against Core's V2ContinueAsNewOpenChildSupervisionTest and V2WorkflowTaskBridgeTest cases.
